feature: Icon snapping reaches what the icon mock draws
summary: Inside an icon frame, boxes, ovals and lines now land on whole units like Pen points do, every drawn shape's corners, edges and centre pull the next one, a blue pill beside the landing ring names the spot in the icon's units, and View > Snap in Icons turns Grid, Keylines and Geometry on or off.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/shapes-snap-in-an-icon-walk.json

try.do: Choose File > New Frame, pick 24 under Icons, click Add Frame, then zoom to 800%.
Pick Rectangle and hover over the icon: a ring marks where the corner will land and a pill beside it reads 9, 10.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the box out: the pill follows the far corner and reads the whole-unit spot it will stop on.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick Ellipse and drag a circle; then hover near the box's top left corner: the ring jumps onto the corner even where plain rounding would not.
Hover just right of the circle's edge: the ring sits on that edge and the pill names it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open View > Snap in Icons and untick Geometry: the same hover now rounds to the nearest unit instead.
Edit > Copy the icon and paste the SVG somewhere: every box and oval is in whole numbers.

evaluate: Does the pill beside the ring tell you where the point will land before you press, without getting in the way of what you are aiming at?
Do shapes pull the next shape firmly enough at 800%, or does an edge catch a point you meant to put one unit away?
Is View > Snap in Icons where you would look for these switches?
Should a new icon frame start with all three pulls on, as now, or with snapping off as the mock's status line shows?
rough: The mock's Grid & snap group sits in the right panel; the Snap to choices are View > Snap in Icons > Grid, Keylines, Geometry instead, because snapping is a View menu row (UX-PATTERNS placement contract). Where the grid's own controls live is the open card on the-grid-s-controls-come-back-to-the-tool-bar-as.

The mock says Control suspends snapping; the app still uses Command, as everywhere on the canvas. That is decision card icon-snapping-reaches-what-the-icon-mock-draws-which-key-lets-a-point-inside-an.
The mock marks the landing spot with an accent cross; the app keeps its own landing ring (the-grid-line-under-a-pen-point-lights-up-while) and adds the mock's pill beside it.

The mock drags its circles out from their centres; the app draws corner to corner, so the mock's step 6 circle is drawn from 6, 7 to 12, 13 to centre it on the corner. Filed as a-box-or-circle-can-be-drawn-out-from-its-centre.

The mock starts with snapping off and turns all three on together; here all three are on from the start, as pen-points-in-an-icon-frame-land-on-whole-units settled (whole units with nothing to switch on).
At 800% a pull reaches three quarters of a unit, so the centre keyline caught a box corner the walk aimed at 12.6 and landed it on 12, not 13. That is the rule, but it is strong.
A line or arrow held at 45 degrees with Shift inside an icon does not land on whole units, because the angle decides its far end.
Window pictures were taken with the probe behind another app; colours of picked controls show their background look.
